title: The Birth of the Monkey King
lines: Five hundred years passed. The Tang Emperor Taizong dreamed of salvation, and the Bodhisattva Guanyin traveled to the mortal world to find someone worthy of undertaking the journey to the West — a pilgrimage to retrieve sacred Buddhist scriptures from India.

Guanyin appeared before Sun Wukong's prison. 'Monkey,' she said, 'I can free you. But in return, you must protect a holy monk on his journey to the West. You will be his disciple.' Sun Wukong, hungry for freedom, agreed.

She gave him a golden fillet — a circlet that would tighten around his head whenever the monk chanted a certain sutra. 'This will remind you to behave,' she said. Sun Wukong, not understanding the trap, nodded eagerly.

The Tang monk, Tripitaka, was a devout Buddhist of extraordinary compassion — and extraordinary naivety. He climbed the Mountain of the Five Elements and found the monkey buried up to his head. 'Master,' Sun Wukong called, 'free me and I shall serve you.'

Tripitaka climbed the cliff and, with trembling hands, removed the Buddha's seal that held the mountain in place. The earth shook. The mountain split. Sun Wukong exploded into the sky, free at last. He prostrated himself before the monk. 'Disciple Sun Wukong greets Master.'

Their first test came when six bandits attacked them on the road. Sun Wukong killed all six with a single sweep of his staff. Tripitaka was horrified. 'You took lives! How can a monk travel with a murderer?' Furious, Sun Wukong flew away.

But Guanyin had prepared for this. When Sun Wukong returned, she and Tripitaka tricked him into putting on the golden fillet — disguised as an innocent cap. The moment it touched his head, it fused to his skull.

Tripitaka chanted the sutra. The fillet tightened. Sun Wukong screamed, clawing at his head. The pain was unimaginable. He fell to his knees, begging. Tripitaka stopped chanting, and the pain ceased. Sun Wukong understood: he was bound.
And so, five hundred years after challenging Heaven, the Monkey King bowed to a mortal monk. Thus began the greatest pilgrimage in all of myth — the journey to the West.
